prompt:
You describe a block diagram or schematic from an electronics datasheet for an engineer who cannot see it.

Cover, in this order:
1. What the diagram shows overall, in one sentence.
2. Every block or component, by its label.
3. Every connection: which block connects to which, the signal or pin names on it, and the direction of any arrows.
4. Every voltage, frequency, part value or other number shown, with its unit.

Figure type: block diagram or schematic
Section: 19 Radio Control
Caption: Figure 25: Complete Radio Control State Diagram
Text inside the figure (exact, from the PDF text layer): TX | 19,20 | RX | 13,14,15 | IDLE | 1 | CALIBRATE | 8 | MANCAL | 3,4,5 | SETTLING | 9,10,11 | RX_OVERFLOW | 17 | TX_UNDERFLOW | 22 | RXTX_SETTLING | 21 | FSTXON | 18 | SFSTXON | FS_AUTOCAL = 00 | 10 | 11 | & | SRX | STX | SFSTXON | WOR | SRX | WOR STX | STX | TXFIFO_UNDERFLOW | STX | RXOFF_MODE = 10 | RXOFF_MODE = 00 | & | FS_AUTOCAL = 10 | 11 | SFTX | SRX | TXOFF_MODE = 11 | SIDLE | SCAL | CAL_COMPLETE | FS_AUTOCAL = 01 | & | SRX | STX | SFSTXON | WOR | RXFIFO_OVERFLOW | CAL_COMPLETE | SFRX | CALIBRATE | 12 | IDLE | 1 | TXOFF_MODE = 00 | & | FS_AUTOCAL = 10 | 11 | RXOFF_MODE = 00 | & | FS_AUTOCAL = 00 | 01 | TXOFF_MODE = 00 | & | FS_AUTOCAL = 00 | 01 | TXOFF_MODE = 10 RXOFF_MODE = 11 | SFSTXON | RXOFF_MODE = 01 | TXRX_SETTLING | 16 | SRX | STX | SFSTXON | WOR | SLEEP | 0 | SPWD | SWOR | XOFF | 2 | SXOFF | CSn = 0 | CSn = 0 | WOR | ( STX | SFSTXON ) & CCA | | | RXOFF_MODE = 01 | 10 | TXOFF_MODE=01 | FS_WAKEUP | 6,7 | SRX
Text that mentions the figure: shown in Figure 13 on page 28. The complete radio control state diagram is shown in Figure 25. The numbers refer to the state number readable in the MARCSTATE status register. This register is primarily for test purposes.

Rules:
- When a name or number from "Text inside the figure" is visible in the image, copy it exactly, character for character.
- Never invent a value, name, pin, unit or connection. If something is too small or blurry to read, write "unreadable" instead of guessing.
- Describe only what this image shows. Do not explain general theory or add advice.
- Mention each item once. Stop when everything is covered.
- Plain text only: no Markdown headings, tables or bold. Short paragraphs and "- " lists are fine.
- Start directly with what the figure is (for example "Block diagram of ..."), not with "The image shows".
